Consult Summary:
19-year-old female with 3-day history of dysuria, mild hematuria and lower abdominal discomfort; telehealth assessment suggests simple cystitis. Empiric 3-day oral antibiotic course and supportive measures advised with safety-net instructions.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis)
- Onset: burning/stinging pain with urination for 3 days.
- Associated symptoms: occasional mild lower abdominal cramp, small amount of blood in urine earlier today, malodorous urine. No urinary frequency, flank/back pain, nausea, vomiting, or fever.
- Sexual history: sexually active with one partner (2 months), uses condoms, never had STI screen; last menstrual period “a couple of weeks ago.” Unlikely pregnant but advised to test if doubt.
- Pertinent negatives: no vaginal discharge, no bowel changes.
- Impression: Simple lower UTI.

Issue 2: Drug allergy – Clindamycin
- Reaction: swelling (suggests possible angio-edema).

Issue 3: Preventive sexual health / contraceptive counselling
- No prior STI screening; advised barrier contraception and temporary abstinence during infection treatment.
- Potential need for pregnancy testing if symptoms persist or concern arises.

Medications:
- Nitrofurantoin OR Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact dose/route not documented).
- OTC bicarbonate previously tried; ineffective.

Allergies:
- Clindamycin – swelling.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).

Social History:
- Lives in shared college flat.
- College student (studying biology).
- Non-smoker.
- Social alcohol use on weekends.

Preventative History:
- No STI screen to date.
- Other routine preventive care not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals recorded (telehealth).
- No physical examination performed.

Plan:
- Start prescribed 3-day oral antibiotic course (Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim).
- Increase oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.
- Avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.
- Red-flag advice: seek review for fever, flank/back pain, increasing abdominal pain, or general deterioration.
- Follow-up: contact clinic if no improvement by end of week or earlier if worsening.
- Consider pregnancy test if any possibility of pregnancy.
- Arrange first comprehensive STI screen at convenient opportunity.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: vital signs, physical examination findings, full antibiotic dose/route, medication reconciliation beyond current list, detailed family history beyond GU/GI.  
● No internal transcript conflicts of clinical significance (minor variation in “couple” vs “three” weeks for LMP).  
● Transcript quality: clear; occasional inaudible/overlapping speech but clinical content intact.
